Ram Bharat vs State Of Mah. Thr. M.N. Ratnaparkhi on 1 July,
2024 
Author: G. A. Sanap Bench: G. A. Sanap 2024:BHC-NAG:7113  18.cri.wp.4  1  IN THE HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT BOMBAY  NAGPUR BENCH, NAGPUR. 
 CRIMINAL WRIT PETITION NO. 486 OF 2023  M/s. Ram Bharat,
 Aged about 44 Yrs., Occupier of  Patanjali Foods Limited, Having  its address at Survey No. 178,
 Surkandi Road, Washim, Taluka  District Washim   // V E R S U S //
 1. State of Maharashtra,
 Through Mr. M. N. Ratnaparkhi,
 Deputy Director, Industrial Safety and  Health, Akola  Amended as  per courts 2. State of Maharashtra,
 order dt.
 13.07.2023  Through its office at  and deleted Advocates for the State of  respondent Maharashtra, High Court,
 no.2  Nagpur   -------------------------------------------------------------------
 Mr. Kushal Mor alongwith Mr Apoorv Shrivastava and Mr R. R.
 Advocates for the petitioner  Mrs H. S. Dhande, APP for respondent No.1/State  -------------------------------------------------------------------
 CORAM : G. A. SANAP, J.
Ram Bharat vs State Of Mah. Thr. M.N. Ratnaparkhi on 1 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153510493/
1  DATE : 01/07/2024  ORAL JUDGMENT :
 1 Heard.
 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt 2 RULE. Rule made returnable forthwith. Taken up for final disposal with the consent of learned Advocates for the parties. 
3 The petitioner has been facing the prosecution in a complaint case under Section 7A(2)(a) read with Section 92 of the Factories Act, 1948 (For short ' the Factories Act'). The complainant is the Deputy Director and Inspector, Industrial Safety and Health, Akola, appointed as per the Factories Act. The accused is the occupier of Ruchi Soya Industries Limited, situated at Survey No. 178,
Surkandi Road, Washim, Taluka and District Washim. The accident in question occurred on 16.08.2021. It is stated that on 16.08.2021 desolventizing of the plant by circulating the hot caustic solution was carried out. At about 12:30 a.m. (midnight) on 16.08.2021 when the caustic circulation was continuing in the solvent extraction plant, operator Shri Pradip Kushwah observed choking in the 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt evaporator pipeline through the glass flow meter provided on the pipeline. He immediately informed this to the shift incharge and they decided to clear the chocking by giving external water pressure by a pipe into the evaporator pipeline. Operator Shri Pradip Kushwah opened the glass flow meter with the help of assistant operator Shri Vijaykumar Rajput and moved the flexible plastic pipe into the evaporator pipeline in an upward direction. He moved this pipe in up and down direction multiple times to give external water pressure to clear the choking. It is alleged that suddenly within 10 minutes, when the chocking was cleared, the hot caustic solution came down with pressure and came out through the open glass flow meter and splashed over on operator Shri Pradip Kushwah and assistant operator Shri Vijaykumar Rajput, who were standing in front of the glass flow meter. They sustained burn injuries. They succumbed to the burn injuries. The shift incharge immediately informed the Manager. It is stated that by 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt undertaking the process of clearing the choking, the risk was invited. There were likely chances of the workers coming into contact with hot chemicals. Proper protective equipments were not provided. The system of work in the factory was not safe and with a risk to the health of the workers. It is alleged that if a proper system of work was adopted and suitable PPES were provided to the deceased worker on the day of the accident, this accident would not have occurred. It is stated that this amounts to a contravention of the provisions of Section 7A(2)
Ram Bharat vs State Of Mah. Thr. M.N. Ratnaparkhi on 1 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153510493/
2 (a) of the Factories Act.
4 On these averments, the complaint came to be filed in the Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Washim. Learned CJM vide order dated 10.11.2021 made over the complaint to the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class-2, Washim. Learned JMFC-2, Washim on 10.11.2021 passed the order of issuance of summons to the accused. The 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt petitioner / accused has come before this Court against this order. 
5 Heard learned Advocate Mr Kushal Mor for the petitioner and learned APP Ms H. S. Dhande for the State/respondent No.1. Perused the record and proceedings. 6 A number of grounds have been raised in the petition. Learned Advocate for the petitioner however confined his arguments to the only ground namely that the order of issuance of a process is mechanical order inasmuch as it does not reflect the application of mind. It is further stated that the learned Magistrate has not recorded his prima facie satisfaction about the offences made out and the reasons for the same. In support of this submission, the learned Advocate has placed reliance on the decision in the case of Lalankumar Singh and others .v / s. State of Maharashtra 1, wherein the 1 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1383 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the words "sufficient ground for proceeding" appearing in Section 204 of the Code of Criminal Procedure are of immense importance. It is these words which amply suggest that an opinion is to be formed only after due application of mind that there is sufficient basis for proceeding against the said accused and the formation of such an opinion is to be stated in the order itself. It is held that if the order is passed mechanically, then such an order cannot be sustained. The Apex Court has held that the Court may not be required to record the detailed reasons, but the reasons recorded must be sufficient to indicate the application of mind by the Court before passing the order.
7 On perusal of the order passed by the learned Magistrate I am fully satisfied that the learned Magistrate has failed to exercise his power in a proper manner. Learned Magistrate mechanically passed the order of issuance of 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt summons. Learned Magistrate has not recorded his reasons for passing the order of issuance of summons. Learned Magistrate was required to record brief reasons as to how he was prima facie satisfied about the disclosure of the offence on the basis of the facts stated in the complaint. The order passed by the learned Magistrate indicates that before passing the order a proper inquiry was not made. The order, in my opinion, reflects the casual approach of the Magistrate. It was passed mechanically. Therefore, in my view, this order is required to be set aside. 
8 The next important question is with regard to the course to be adopted after setting aside the said order. There are two options. One, to quash the proceedings in entirety or second to grant the Magistrate one opportunity to rectify this patent illegality. In my opinion, while choosing one of the options, the Court has to take a holistic view of the matter. 
Ram Bharat vs State Of Mah. Thr. M.N. Ratnaparkhi on 1 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153510493/
3 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt Perusal of the complaint would show that the necessary facts to establish the basic ingredients of the offence have not been set out. The place and address of the residence of the accused has been mentioned in the title of the complaint as Washim. However, the address mentioned in Form-1 is of Uttarakhand. This document was filed with the complaint. In view of this, the learned Magistrate ought to have conducted the inquiry as contemplated under Section 202 before issuing the process. It appears that this aspect has also not been dealt with. In the said accident, two workers lost their lives. In my view, in such a case, even if it is found that there is some mistake while passing an order, an endeavor must be to do the complete justice by granting an opportunity to rectify such mistake. It is necessary to state that in this case, a mistake was committed by the learned Magistrate. The complainant or any other person could not be held responsible for this mistake. In my view, therefore, the complaint, on account of this illegal order passed 18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt by the Magistrate, cannot be quashed outrightly. It will cause prejudice to the complainant, who ultimately is prosecuting the case of the two workers, who have succumbed to the injuries. In view of this, it would be appropriate to set aside the order and remand the matter back to the learned Magistrate for passing the appropriate order in accordance with the law. Accordingly, the petition is partly allowed. 9 The order dated 10.11.2021 passed by the learned Magistrate issuing summons to the accused is quashed & set aside. 
10 The matter is remanded back to the learned Magistrate. Learned Magistrate shall proceed further with the complaint in accordance with law, before passing the order of issuance of summons or process. 
18.cri.wp.486.2023judgment.odt 11 Rule accordingly. The writ petition stands disposed of,
accordingly.
(G. A. SANAP, J.) Namrata Signed by: Miss Namrata Suryawanshi Designation: PA To Honourable Judge Date: 08/07/2024 19:02:30 Ram Bharat vs State Of Mah. Thr. M.N. Ratnaparkhi on 1 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153510493/
